learning_outcomes.text: Apply the knowledge acquired in the degree to biomechanical studies used in research and/or companies.
Integrate all their knowledge to identify, formulate and solve multidisciplinary problems related to biomechanics.
Evaluate the kinematic and dynamic behavior of the musculoskeletal system.
Understand the mechanical behavior of different biological tissues, both hard and soft.
Manage bibliography, documentation, legislation, databases, specific software and hardware applied to biomechanics.
Use the experimental techniques and engineering tools necessary for solving problems in the biomechanical field.
Design and conduct experimental tests in biomechanics, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Interact with commercial finite element programs through Python and/or MATLAB code programming.
Develop numerical finite element models and interpret the results correctly.
Communicate their conclusions and knowledge to specialized biomechanics audiences.
Adequate knowledge of their engineering branch, including some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
The ability to perform bibliographic searches, use databases and other sources of information.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering to meet required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Multidisciplinary application of biomechanics (medicine, sport, ergonomics, road safety, etc.)
3D printing and its applications in biomechanics
Applications: gait biomechanics, occupational biomechanics, impact biomechanics
The finite element method in biomechanics
Design and manufacture of customized prostheses
assessment_rules: To pass the course, attendance at practicals is mandatory. Continuous assessment components are: partial theoretical exams (30%), course practicals (20%), and biomechanical application project (50%). Students who do not pass via continuous assessment can take an ordinary exam, where continuous assessment counts for 40% and the ordinary exam for 60%. In the extraordinary assessment, the final grade will be the maximum of (40% continuous assessment + 60% extraordinary final exam) or (100% extraordinary final exam).
